proposals.economic_premise: A broad, survivorship-aware cryptocurrency spot basket may earn a market risk premium, while realized risk changes faster than expected return. Holding less cash-funded spot exposure after high measured volatility may improve geometric compounding and drawdown without forecasting which coin has the strongest price path.
proposals.expected_payoff_source: Compensation for broad cryptocurrency market risk combined with lower exposure during high-variance states; this is not an arbitrage claim.
proposals.ex_ante_directional_prediction: A fixed, unlevered inverse-variance exposure rule should retain positive cost-net returns while improving drawdown or risk-adjusted performance versus a preregistered static broad-spot benchmark.

primary_sources.title: Volatility-Managed Portfolios
primary_sources.relevance: Establishes the ex-ante premise that scaling market exposure down when volatility rises can improve risk-adjusted compounding.

primary_sources.title: Common Risk Factors in Cryptocurrency
primary_sources.relevance: Supports treating broad cryptocurrency market exposure as a distinct priced factor without validating any Aurex implementation.

proposals.decision_rationale: It is the only proposal with two supporting primary sources, complete current point-in-time data, current long-only spot expressibility, no leverage requirement, low expected turnover, and no dependency on a retired Aurex signal or R4 outcome bucket.

proposals.economic_premise: Asymmetric realized jump variation may proxy investor attention and priced jump risk. Coins with different ex-ante signed-jump exposure may therefore have different subsequent expected returns independently of endpoint momentum or path-quality ranking.
proposals.expected_payoff_source: Compensation or mispricing associated with asymmetric jump risk and attention to unusually discontinuous price moves.
proposals.ex_ante_directional_prediction: A preregistered cross-sectional sort on signed-jump variation should produce a stable cost-net return difference in the direction declared by the primary crypto study.

primary_sources.title: Good Volatility, Bad Volatility: Signed Jumps and the Persistence of Volatility
primary_sources.relevance: Defines the high-frequency signed-jump and realized-semivariance foundation required to test the proposed jump-risk mechanism.

primary_sources.title: Good Volatility, Bad Volatility, and the Cross Section of Cryptocurrency Returns
primary_sources.relevance: Provides a crypto-specific premise that realized signed jump variation may contain cross-sectional return information.

proposals.decision_rationale: The mechanism is distinct and research-supported, but approximating its defining high-frequency statistic from four-hour candles would change the mechanism before it is tested.

proposals.economic_premise: Persistent futures basis and perpetual funding can compensate a hedged trader for supplying balance sheet and convergence capital. The payoff is structurally different from forecasting spot-price direction, but remains exposed to basis, collateral, venue, and liquidation risk.
proposals.expected_payoff_source: Funding and basis paid by directional or leverage-constrained perpetual-futures demand to a spot-perpetual hedged position.
proposals.ex_ante_directional_prediction: A fully costed and collateralized spot-long/perpetual-short position should earn positive net carry only when prospective funding exceeds fees, basis slippage, financing, and tail-risk reserves.

primary_sources.title: The Crypto Carry Trade
primary_sources.relevance: Documents the economic basis for hedged spot-futures carry while leaving venue, collateral, basis, and liquidation risk unresolved.

primary_sources.title: Fundamentals of Perpetual Futures
primary_sources.relevance: Provides the perpetual-futures pricing and funding mechanics needed to define carry, hedge slippage, and basis risk.

proposals.decision_rationale: The premise is economically distinct, but selecting it now would require unqualified derivatives execution, leverage, liquidation modeling, and historical datasets that Aurex has not frozen.
